question.title: How many public releases will U.S. Central Command publish on its official Public Releases page dated between 8/1/2026 and 8/10/2026?
question.description:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) publishes official public releases — strike announcements, interdiction reports, casualty statements, and operational updates — on its Public Releases page at [https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/.](https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/.) Release tempo tracks the intensity of U.S. operations against Iran and Iran-backed forces.

Data context (as of 7/29/2026): rolling 10-day release counts over the past six weeks have swung widely — about 4 (6/19-6/28), 3 (6/29-7/8), 11 (7/9-7/18), and 8 (7/19-7/28). At the mid-July peak, CENTCOM published roughly 15 releases in 13 days during nightly strike waves. Beginning 7/24/2026 the United States paused strikes — four consecutive days with no new release, reported as intended to give mediated peace talks space — while Iran publicly denies that any negotiations are underway. Publications resumed 7/28/2026 with a release on a U.S.-Saudi strike against Iran-backed targets in Iraq, and the naval blockade affecting Iranian ports remains in force. Whether August tempo resembles the June lull, the mid-July peak, or something between is the open question.
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the integer count of distinct public releases listed on U.S. Central Command's official English-language Public Releases page (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/) whose displayed publication date falls between 8/1/2026 and 8/10/2026 inclusive, as observed on 8/11/2026 at approximately 12:00 UTC. Each distinct release listed with an in-window date counts exactly once, regardless of subject, length, or type (strike announcements, interdiction or maritime reports, casualty or personnel statements, joint statements, and operational updates all count equally). The displayed publication date on the listing governs; releases dated outside the window do not count regardless of their subject. Items appearing only on CENTCOM's non-English sub-pages, on social media, on DVIDS, or in press briefings/transcripts that are not listed as entries on the Public Releases page do not count. If more than 20 qualifying releases are listed, the question resolves above the upper bound (the range's upper bound is open for this outcome). A count of 0 resolves to 0 (the lower bound is closed at zero, the physical floor). Releases added to the page after the 8/11/2026 observation, or whose displayed dates are changed after observation, do not alter the resolution. If [www.centcom.mil](https://www.centcom.mil) is unavailable at the observation time, the resolver should retry periodically through 8/11/2026 23:59 UTC; if it remains unavailable, the count is taken from the most recent Internet Archive Wayback Machine capture of the Public Releases page taken on or after 8/10/2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/2026\*/centcom.mil/MEDIA/PUBLIC-RELEASES/), applying the same rules. If neither the live page nor any qualifying archive capture is available by 8/12/2026 12:00 UTC, the question is annulled.
